analysis: Examined all units. (1) StandaloneServer.swift (head 1776-2304): the ensureModelLoaded flow. The visible portion is the load path with CBv2 adapter guard, pending-load lease, weight-hash bracketing and post-build headroom guards. The diff elsewhere threads minimumGrantBytes into resliceGrants and adds a static helper; the visible excerpt contains no change to hash verification, cache eligibility or the SSD cache binding (T-041). The cache-eligible weight hash is still only set from the bracketed pre/post hash decision. Whether EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants honors the new minimumGrantBytes parameter correctly was not in the supplied evidence (availability/KV-grant concern, T-029 class); it is an unverified contract, not a finding. (2) ClusterServiceAgent.swift: adds partHealthPath, a pure path helper (part-health.json beside service-health.json). No file I/O, no new privilege; the consumer of this path (ClusterService.partEnvironment) is outside the supplied batch. (3) ClusterRuntimeFactsCommand.swift: adds --release-candidates and --list-release-models modes to a hidden metadata-only CLI. It reads local metadata and writes canonical bytes to stdout and notes to stderr. It performs no network access, key use or secret access. The command validates option exclusivity and round-trips the output through the strict decoder before emitting it. The release-lane trust (running the final signed app's CLI) and the ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.release/candidates implementations are outside the supplied evidence. (4) ClusterSetupWizardCommand.swift: a single line sets service.wizard.servingScope = request.scope. How servingScope is consumed (whether it widens serving scope or bypasses authorization, TB-011/T-052) is not visible, so it is flagged for integration review, not as a finding. No concrete security regression is identified from the supplied lines.
